API reference

The pages under reference/ are generated by TypeDoc from the built packages: one page per package and one per entry point, listing every exported function, class, interface, and type with its signature, doc comment, and a link to the source line.

Do not edit anything under reference/ by hand. Regenerate it from the repository root after changing a public signature or doc comment:

pnpm docs:api

The generator reads each package's source entry point through typedoc.json at the repository root and rewrites docs/api/reference/ in full. This page is the only hand-written file in docs/api/.

Packages

PackageWhat it exportsReference
@axe/coreThe server runtime: createAXE, action, the result helpers (needsInput, handoff, pending, and the error helper), kinds and accept, token and idempotency stores, JSON Pointer utilities, the wire types. No framework dependencies.@axe/core
@axe/clientThe agent side: AXEClient with discover, invoke, continue, resume, poll, and run, plus fulfillers and status type guards. No runtime dependencies.@axe/client
@axe/mcpA Model Context Protocol server derived from an AXE server, manifest, or URL: createMcpServer, serveStdio, serveHttp.@axe/mcp
@axe/expressaxeExpress for Express 4 and 5 and Connect-style frameworks, plus Node-to-Web request and response converters other Node adapters reuse.@axe/express
@axe/nextaxeNext for App Router route files, axeNextPages for the Pages API.@axe/next
@axe/fetchaxeFetch for Hono, Remix, Cloudflare Workers, Bun, Deno, and SvelteKit, plus a path predicate for routers.@axe/fetch
@axe/testingrunConformance, runAudit and its weights, createTestClient for in-process tests, checkVocabularyDrift, sample payloads for every well-known kind.@axe/testing
@axe/surfacecreateSurface (a registry of live controls with observe, act, and one revision), useSurface for React, and surfaceActions, which serves any surface as AXE actions with refusals mapped onto the ladder.@axe/surface, react, axe
@axe/generatefromOpenAPI, fromFunctions, and fromTRPCRouter yield action candidates from definitions an application already has; generate applies overrides and policy, runs the honesty lints, and returns actions with provenance and warnings; registerGenerated registers them.@axe/generate
axeThe CLI: axe init, axe validate, axe inspect, axe preview, axe conformance, axe audit, axe mcp, axe generate. The reference covers its programmatic surface; the commands are in Getting started.axe

Entry points of @axe/core

The main entry point re-exports the runtime and the most-used pieces of each subpath. The subpaths exist so agent-side and tooling code can import types or constants without pulling in Zod.

  • @axe/core/kinds — kinds, the typed well-known kind definitions; accept to build a requirement from one; helpers for custom x- kinds.
  • @axe/core/events — the event type and the platform-neutral sinks: consoleSink, otelSink, combineSinks.
  • @axe/core/node — jsonlFileSink, the one export that needs Node. Nothing else in the package reaches for a built-in, so a browser bundle never meets one.
  • @axe/core/json-schema — validateJsonSchema and the schema helpers, with no Zod; @axe/surface validates through this entry.
  • @axe/core/display — resolveDisplay, which applies a display declaration to an output and returns a presented result.
  • @axe/core/lint — lintAgentText and lintManifest, and the patterns they match.
  • @axe/core/schemas — Zod schemas for every wire object, for validating documents you did not generate.
  • @axe/core/vocabulary — the WIRE constant: every path, header, status, error code, kind, field, and CLI name as a typed string.
  • @axe/core/types — the wire-level TypeScript types, with no runtime code.

Where to start

Integrating a site. Read createAXE and action in the @axe/core index; together they are most of the API. Then kinds and accept in @axe/core/kinds for requirements, and needsInput and handoff for the escalation ladder. Your framework's adapter is one function with one options object.

Building an agent. Start with AXEClient in the @axe/client index: discover finds a manifest from any URL, run drives the whole ladder with fulfillers and confirmation. Then @axe/client/present: present applies a display to a result, and toMarkdown or toHTML renders it.

The vocabulary is generated

WIRE in @axe/core/vocabulary is generated from spec/VOCABULARY.md, not written by hand. A test regenerates it and fails if the committed file differs; the drift test fails if a wire name in the docs is missing from the vocabulary. To add or rename a wire name, edit the spec table and regenerate.
